reconstructed_theorem_text: For every measurable space X, every sigma-finite measure mu on X, and all functions f,g:X->R, assume that f is measurable and that both x->exp(f(x)) and x->exp(g(x)) are mu-integrable. Define Z_f = integral exp(f(z)) dmu(z) and Z_g = integral exp(g(z)) dmu(z), and let mu_f = mu.tilted(f) and mu_g = mu.tilted(g), the normalized exponential reweightings specified by the tilted-measure construction. Then the selected measurable real log-likelihood-ratio representative llr(mu_f,mu_g) satisfies llr(mu_f,mu_g)(x) = f(x)-log(Z_f)-g(x)+log(Z_g) for mu_f-almost every x. Here exp and log are the real exponential and the Lean real logarithm. The almost-everywhere reference measure is mu_f, not an unstated background probability measure. No separate global measurability assumption on g, nonzero-mass assumption on mu, or positive-normalizer assumption is imposed; the statement uses the Lean constructions also in degenerate cases and does not assert a pointwise identity.
